content: I'll start by reading the test image to analyze the disease symptoms.

The test image shows a tomato plant with severe whole-plant collapse/wilt on black plastic mulch. The left portion shows completely wilted, collapsed stems with dried foliage, while the right portion shows actively wilting leaves. This is a sudden, complete wilt pattern suggesting a vascular or bacterial disease.

Key visual features:
- Whole-plant wilting/collapse
- Stems appear to have lost structural integrity
- No obvious leaf spots or lesions visible
- Sudden wilt pattern consistent with vascular disruption

This pattern strongly suggests bacterial wilt. Let me view a reference image to confirm.

The reference image for Bacterial_Wilt shows the classic bacterial streaming diagnostic test (milky threads from stem cross-section in water), confirming this is vascular bacterial disease.

**Analysis comparison:**

**Test image:** Whole tomato plant collapsed/lying flat on black plastic mulch. Left portion completely wilted and desiccated, right portion actively wilting. No visible leaf spots, no basal rot, no white mycelium at soil line. Sudden, complete whole-plant collapse.

**Bacterial_Wilt reference:** Shows vascular browning and bacterial streaming from stem cross-section — the hallmark of *Ralstonia solanacearum*.

**Reasoning:**
- The sudden, complete whole-plant wilt without leaf spots or lesions is characteristic of Bacterial Wilt
- No white mycelial mat at soil line (rules out Southern Blight)
- No gradual bottom-up yellowing (rules out Verticillium Wilt)
- No basal stem rot (rules out Rhizopus/Sclerotinia)
- The collapse pattern — rapid, entire plant, wilting without chlorosis — fits bacterial vascular occlusion
